checks: Real Terminal cp -R/mv copy and move nested folders; pbcopy/pbpaste exchange actual shared text
Finder context Copy/Paste transfers a real file across distinct Finder windows without deleting source
Finder context Cut/Paste moves a directory with nested files across windows through the real atomic move syscall
Real held-button drag drops a file onto a directory icon, changing the actual filesystem
Real drag to Finder sidebar moves into Desktop
Ctrl-drag across two positioned Finder windows copies rather than moves and generates a non-overwriting collision name
Desktop file icons can be dragged into an open Finder destination, and Finder files can be dropped onto the bare Desktop
Real drag into Terminal inserts a quoted path into the pending command; only an explicit Enter executes it
Terminal Ctrl+Shift+C/V uses shared clipboard while paste only edits input, never auto-executes
Session lock clears the shared clipboard; old Finder/Terminal buffers cannot repaste the previous shared content
Copied/moved folders and drag results persist through a cold installed boot and full data/system verification
